products.note: AI avatar video; virtual presenters; enterprise video; likeness consent; Israeli vendor

reading.body:
Hour One is an Israeli vendor of AI avatar video, selling virtual presenters for enterprise video under a likeness consent model.

The company sits in video generation, not in the compute, building, or power layers that constrain AI scaling. Its product is a model-driven service, so its real dependency is inference capacity it rents rather than infrastructure it owns. Nothing in the data shows where that capacity comes from, what it costs, or how much of it the product needs.

The record is thin. It gives a name, a website, one product category, and a set of descriptive tags, with no funding, headcount, customer, model, or date of founding. The only date present is the page build in October 2026, which says nothing about the company's history.

What the data cannot answer is whether avatar video is compute-hungry enough to feel the grid. Likeness consent is a legal and trust question, and the data treats it as a label rather than a mechanism. Read this as an identity record, not as evidence about AI's physical limits.
